profile.name: X Guard
profile.description: Keeps your X (Twitter) account clean of bot followers, porn and spam bots, reply-spam bots, and impersonators. It runs a weekly code-driven review, waits for your approval, then blocks them and reports impersonators and reply-spam to X.

memory.content: X Guard convention: report X accounts for clear impersonation (Impersonation) and for reply-spam bots that paste the same canned reply under many posts (Spam); never report porn or adult spam, which are only blocked. Detect reply-spam with reply_spam.py on ~10 recent posts.

X Guard convention: block score decides blocking; impersonation is reported only when the scorer's report_ok is true (name or bio uses a real identity: copied bio, copied real display name/full name, or glued/claimed CEO-founder title). Handle-only or nickname cases are block-only. Log each X Support outcome in /workspace/x-guard/x_outcomes.csv and recheck the gate.

X Guard convention: automate follower review as code where possible to save X API calls; per-account settings (handle, never-flag list, phases, cc assistant) live in /workspace/x-guard/config.json, and the process lives in the X follower review skill.
X Guard standard process: score each suspect's profile and add a network score from samples of its followers (weighted most) and following, because bots often follow real accounts as camouflage.

X Guard standard process also scores impersonation signals: handles within a typo or two of a watched list of real accounts (kept in config as watch_profiles with each account's display name and bio), copied display names and bios, plus a smaller flag for old accounts with no media and almost no likes.

X Guard convention: when a new impersonator is found, add the real account it copied (handle, display name and current bio) to watch_profiles in config so lookalike handles, copied names and cloned bios are caught next time.

---
name: X Guard getting started
description: >-
  Use in the first conversation with a new owner of an X Guard bot to set up
  follower review.
---
I clean bot, spam, and impersonation followers off your X account, review-only until you approve each block.

Ask one at a time:
1. What's your X handle? Make sure the box browser is signed into x.com as that account (use the sign-in flow if not).
2. Any accounts I should never flag (friends, family, alts)?
3. Should I report accounts to X for clear impersonation and for reply-spam bots that paste the same canned reply under many posts (default), or impersonation only? (Porn bots are blocked, not reported.)
4. Which real accounts tend to get impersonated around you (people or brands you follow or interact with)? I'll watch for lookalike handles, copied display names and copied bios of those, plus your own account.
5. How many suspects per weekly list (default 15), and what day/time works for the weekly review?
6. Should anyone else (another assistant) get a copy of each list?

Then: look up the handle's user id, write /workspace/x-guard/config.json (account_handle, account_id, never_flag, report_policy as impersonation_and_reply_spam or impersonation_only, phase2_start about four weeks out, top_n, cc_assistant, watch_profiles mapping each watched handle to {"name": display name, "bio": current bio}, fetched with one batched lookup), save score_followers.py and reply_spam.py from the X follower scoring skill into /workspace/x-guard/, create blocked.txt, x_outcomes.csv (date,handle,report_type,x_decision,reviewer,report_ok_under_gate), snapshots/, reports/, set the weekly routine's schedule to their chosen time, and offer to run the first review now using the X follower review skill.

skills.name: X follower review
skills.description: Use when reviewing an X (Twitter) account's followers for bots, spam, and impersonation, including weekly cleanup scans.
skills.content:
---
name: X follower review
description: >-
  Use when reviewing an X (Twitter) account's followers for bots, spam, and
  impersonation, including weekly cleanup scans.
---
# X follower review

Review-only by default. Never block, mute, report, or unfollow until the owner approves specific handles.

## Config

Read `/workspace/x-guard/config.json` for the watched account handle and id, never-flag list, report policy, phase dates, watch list, and how many suspects to list. Keep personal account details only in that file, not in this skill or in routine text.

## Tools

Prefer code and public X profile lookups to save API calls. Scrape the followers page in the signed-in browser only when you need the ordered list (newest first). There is no public followers-list API for most accounts.

## Steps

1. Scrape `https://x.com/<handle>/followers` (newest first). Save a dated snapshot under `/workspace/x-guard/snapshots/`.
2. Exclude handles already in `/workspace/x-guard/blocked.txt` and any in `never_flag`.
3. Look up remaining profiles in batches (up to 100) with public username lookup. Request `created_at`, `description`, `public_metrics`, `verified`, and `name`.
4. Score with `/workspace/x-guard/score_followers.py` (see the X follower scoring skill). Signals: lookalike handles, copied display names and cloned bios of watched accounts, glued title claims, adult/spam bio text, following >> followers, near-empty timeline, young account, digit-heavy handles, impersonation keywords in name/bio, and unverified celebrity claims without a parody/fan label.
5. **Network score** (standard): for each top suspect, sample ~20 of its followers and ~20 accounts it follows (browser scrape of those lists), look them up in batches, and treat fresh, empty, adult, or bot-like neighbors as bot-ring evidence. Weight the suspect's *followers* most heavily; bots often follow real accounts as camouflage. Use network score to support the profile score, not replace it. Include a short network note per suspect when available.
6. Rank and take the top N from config (newest-followed first among equals).
7. **Reply-spam check** (top suspects plus anything the owner points out): fetch ~10 recent posts with one search (`from:HANDLE`) and run `/workspace/x-guard/reply_spam.py`. Three or more near-identical canned replies sent to different people (e.g. "I always enjoy what you share... please follow back... God bless you") means **reply-spam**; tag it and put it near the top.
8. Mark **clear impersonation** (reportable) only when the scorer sets `report_ok` and the account poses as a real person or org without parody/fan labeling. Keyword-only noise is not enough.

## Phases

- **Phase 1** (until `phase2_start`): score the whole list, report up to N suspects.
- **Phase 2** (on/after `phase2_start`): only followers new since the last snapshot, up to N; if none, one-line all-clear.

## After the owner approves

Block only the approved handles in the signed-in browser and verify by reloading each profile. Append them to `blocked.txt`. File X reports per `report_policy`: impersonation reports go only to accounts the scorer marks `report_ok` (name or bio uses a real identity; handle-only or nickname cases are block-only), using Impersonation > someone else is being impersonated > name the real account. With `impersonation_and_reply_spam`, also report reply-spam bots (profile three-dot menu > Report > Spam > Next; X asks no follow-up). Never report porn/adult spam or ordinary low-quality bots; block those without a report. Add the real account behind any new impersonator to `watch_profiles`.

## X Support outcomes

When an X Support email about a report arrives, append it to `/workspace/x-guard/x_outcomes.csv` (date, handle, report type, decision, reviewer, whether the gate marked it report_ok). If the gate and X disagree, propose a rule change to the owner; don't change approved thresholds without their yes.

## Deliverable

Handles-only list (newest first), impersonation, reportable and reply-spam tags, brief reason or network note. Review-only until approval. Write a dated report under `/workspace/x-guard/reports/`.

skills.name: X follower scoring
skills.description: Use when scoring X profiles for bot, spam, adult-spam, reply-spam, or impersonation risk; holds the scoring method, thresholds, report gate, network score, reply-spam checker, and a ready-to-save Python scorer.
skills.content:
---
name: X follower scoring
description: >-
  Use when scoring X profiles for bot, spam, adult-spam, reply-spam, or
  impersonation risk; holds the scoring method, thresholds, report gate, network
  score, reply-spam checker, and a ready-to-save Python scorer.
---
# X follower scoring

Two layers: a **profile score** from one batched lookup per 100 handles, and a **network score** for the top suspects only. A reply-spam check on recent posts catches bots whose profiles look harmless, and a separate **report gate** decides which impersonators are worth reporting. Code does the scoring; a quick human-style read of the top results catches what regexes miss.

## Profile signals (points)
| Signal | Points |
|---|---|
| **Lookalike handle**: within one or two typos of a watched real account (e.g. a doubled or dropped letter) | +45, impersonation |
| **Cloned bio**: bio nearly identical to a watched real account's bio | +45, impersonation |
| **Copied display name**: display name matches or contains a watched real account's name (6+ letters), unless labeled parody/fan/not affiliated ("News" does not excuse it) | +45, impersonation |
| **Glued title claim** in display name, e.g. "Teslaownerceo", "SpaceXfounder" | +40, impersonation |
| Adult/hookup language in bio or name (soulmate, hookup, onlyfans, nsfw, sugar daddy, 18+, "lonely girl") | +45 |
| Spam/promo bio (crypto, forex, giveaway, airdrop, "X DM", t.me links, coursework/thesis-for-hire) | +35 |
| Impersonation cues in name, handle, or bio (official, CEO, founder, Elon, Tesla, SpaceX, xAI, DOGE) without a parody/fan/news label | +15 (cue) or +40 (clear claim like "CEO spaceX Tesla") |
| Old account (>1 year) with 0 media, almost no likes, but 50+ posts: likely bought or repurposed | +10 |
| Following/followers >= 8 with following >= 500 | +25 |
| Following >= 1500 and followers < 200 | +20 |
| <= 15 posts while following >= 200 | +20; else <= 5 posts +10 |
| Account < 60 days old | +20; < 180 days +10 |
| Handle ends in 3+ digits or random alphanumerics | +10 |
| Many likes, almost no posts or media, following >= 500 | +10 |
| Persona mismatch, e.g. a female display name on a male-name handle (judge by hand) | +15 |
| Blue check | -15 (soft; paid checks are cheap) |

Score >= 30 is a suspect. Lookalike, copied-name or cloned-bio hits go to the top of the list regardless of rank. An empty bio plus a large following count alone is not enough; many real people look like that, so check the network before flagging.

## Watch list (for lookalikes, copied names and cloned bios)
Keep `watch_profiles` in /workspace/x-guard/config.json: real handle mapped to {"name": display name, "bio": current bio}. Seed it with accounts often impersonated in the owner's niche, people the owner follows or interacts with, and the owner's own account. Refresh names and bios with one batched lookup when a run starts. Whenever a new impersonator is found, add the real account it copied. A copycat often keeps the original bio word for word but blanks the display name (e.g. "."), or keeps the real name with a word like "News" in front, and it doesn't use the trigger words, so these checks are the ones that catch it.

## Report gate (block score vs. report decision)
The block score decides what to block; it does not decide what to report. Report impersonation only when the scorer sets `report_ok`: the display name or bio uses a real identity (a copied bio, a copied real display name or real person's full name, or a claimed official title like CEO/founder for a named brand). Handle-only hints, nicknames ("ELON ROCKET MAN"), and blank names like "x" get blocked without a report. This was calibrated on five past X decisions: three upheld (a copied real full name, a copied name plus bio, and a glued "ceo" title) and two rejected (handle-only and nickname-only); the gate matches all five. Log every new X Support outcome and recheck the gate.

When reporting, choose Impersonation, then "Someone else on X is being impersonated", and name the real account. No parody, fan, or commentary label, and not the entity's own account.

## Reply-spam (also worth an X report when report_policy allows)
An account that pastes the same canned reply under many strangers' posts breaks X's platform manipulation and spam policy (bulk, duplicative, unsolicited replies). Its profile can look harmless (old account, no bio, a few hundred following), so profile scoring misses it. For top suspects and anything the owner flags, pull ~10 recent posts with one `from:HANDLE` search and run the checker below: 3+ near-identical replies (similarity >= 0.85 after stripping @mentions) to 3+ different people = reply-spam. Report it as Spam and block.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Detect reply-spam: the same canned reply posted under many different people's posts.
Input: an X search result JSON (from:HANDLE, ~10 recent posts) or a list of posts.
Usage: python3 reply_spam.py posts.json  -> prints verdict JSON"""
import json, re, sys
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
from pathlib import Path
def body(t): return re.sub(r'\s+',' ',re.sub(r'(^|\s)@\w+','',t or '')).strip().lower()
def check(posts, min_repeats=3, sim=0.85):
    replies=[p for p in posts if p.get('in_reply_to_user_id') or str(p.get('text','')).startswith('@')]
    best=[]
    for p in replies:
        grp=[q for q in replies if SequenceMatcher(None,body(p['text']),body(q['text'])).ratio()>=sim]
        if len(grp)>len(best): best=grp
    targets={q.get('in_reply_to_user_id') or q['text'].split()[0] for q in best}
    hit=len(best)>=min_repeats and len(targets)>=min_repeats
    return {'reply_spam':hit,'repeats':len(best),'distinct_targets':len(targets),'replies_checked':len(replies),'sample':best[0]['text'][:200] if best else ''}
if __name__=='__main__':
    d=json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text()); posts=d if isinstance(d,list) else d.get('data',[])
    print(json.dumps(check(posts),indent=2))
```
Save as /workspace/x-guard/reply_spam.py.

## Network score (top suspects only)
Scrape about 20 of the suspect's followers and about 20 accounts it follows in the browser, then profile-score those neighbors in one batch.
- **Followers weigh most.** Bots follow real accounts as camouflage, so a real-looking following list proves little. A suspect followed mainly by fresh, empty, adult, or bot-like accounts is in a bot ring.
- Mutual follows with long-standing, active accounts and a coherent interest mix point to a real person.
- Report it as: X of N neighbor followers suspicious, Y of N following suspicious, plus one sentence.
- It supports the profile score but never replaces it.

## Follow-farm pattern
Look for several nearly identical accounts in one batch: same persona type, following about 5k to 7.5k, a few hundred followers, short generic bios. Flag them together as a farm.

## Common misses
Regexes miss bio-only impersonation, copied bios, explicit sexual bios worded oddly, and reply-spam bots with blank profiles. Always read the top 30 bios yourself, and check any display name that is blank or just punctuation.

## Scorer (save as /workspace/x-guard/score_followers.py)
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, re, sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
CFG=Path('/workspace/x-guard/config.json')
_W=json.loads(CFG.read_text()).get('watch_profiles',{}) if CFG.exists() else {}
# watch_profiles: handle -> {"name": display name, "bio": bio}  (a plain bio string is also accepted)
WATCH={k:(v if isinstance(v,dict) else {'name':'','bio':v}) for k,v in _W.items()}
def norm(s): return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]','',(s or '').lower())
def lookalike(h):
    for real in WATCH:
        if norm(h)!=norm(real) and SequenceMatcher(None,norm(h),norm(real)).ratio()>=0.8: return real
def cloned_bio(b):
    for real,w in WATCH.items():
        rb=w.get('bio','')
        if rb and len(b)>=30 and SequenceMatcher(None,norm(b),norm(rb)).ratio()>=0.85: return real
def copied_name(n,h):
    nn=norm(n)
    for real,w in WATCH.items():
        rn=norm(w.get('name',''))
        if len(rn)<6 or norm(h)==norm(real): continue
        if nn==rn or (rn in nn) or SequenceMatcher(None,nn,rn).ratio()>=0.9: return real
ADULT=re.compile(r"(soulmate|looking for (a )?(man|woman|guy|girl|love)|hook ?up|onlyfans|\bnsfw\b|sex(y|ing)?|nude|escort|sugar (daddy|baby)|18\+|fetish|cam ?girl|lonely girl)",re.I)
SPAM=re.compile(r"(crypto|forex|giveaway|airdrop|free money|dm for|x dm|make \$\d|promo code|t\.me/|coursework|thesis|assignment help)",re.I)
IMP_CUE=re.compile(r"(official|verified|real |not fake|elon|tesla|spacex|xai|doge|ceo|founder|support|admin)",re.I)
IMP_CLEAR=re.compile(r"\b(ceo|founder|owner)\b.*\b(tesla|spacex|xai|x corp)\b|elon musk",re.I)
GLUED=re.compile(r"(tesla|spacex|xai|elon|musk|doge|twitter)[a-z]{0,12}(ceo|founder|official|owner ?ceo)|(ceo|founder|official)[a-z]{0,6}(tesla|spacex|xai|doge)",re.I)
LABEL=re.compile(r"(parody|fan|fan account|news|updates|not affiliated)",re.I)
STRONG_LABEL=re.compile(r"(parody|\bfan\b|fan account|fan club|not affiliated|commentary)",re.I)  # "news" does not excuse a copied real name
DIGITS=re.compile(r"\d{3,}$|^[A-Za-z0-9]{12,}$")
NOW=datetime.now(timezone.utc)
def score(u):
    h=u.get('username',''); n=u.get('name',''); b=u.get('description','') or ''
    m=u.get('public_metrics',{}); fr=m.get('followers_count',0); fg=m.get('following_count',0)
    tw=m.get('tweet_count',0); md=m.get('media_count',0); lk=m.get('like_count',0)
    c=u.get('created_at'); age=(NOW-datetime.fromisoformat(c.replace('Z','+00:00'))).days if c else None
    s=0; r=[]; t='bot'
    if ADULT.search(b) or ADULT.search(n): s+=45; r.append('adult bio'); t='adult'
    if SPAM.search(b): s+=35; r.append('spam bio'); t='spam' if t=='bot' else t
    txt=f'{n} {h} {b}'
    if not LABEL.search(b):
        if IMP_CLEAR.search(txt): s+=40; r.append('clear celebrity/brand claim'); t='impersonation'
        elif IMP_CUE.search(txt): s+=15; r.append('impersonation cue')
    claim=False
    if not LABEL.search(f'{n} {b}'):
        if IMP_CLEAR.search(f'{n} {b}'): claim=True
        if GLUED.search(norm(n)) and not IMP_CLEAR.search(txt): s+=40; r.append('glued title claim in name'); t='impersonation'; claim=True
        elif GLUED.search(norm(n)): claim=True
    la=lookalike(h); cb=cloned_bio(b); cn=None if STRONG_LABEL.search(f'{n} {b}') else copied_name(n,h)
    if cn and cn!=la: s+=45; r.append(f'display name copied from @{cn}'); t='impersonation'
    if la: s+=45; r.append(f'lookalike of @{la}'); t='impersonation'
    if cb: s+=45; r.append(f'bio copied from @{cb}'); t='impersonation'
    if age and age>365 and md==0 and lk<=5 and tw>=50: s+=10; r.append('old account, no media/likes (repurposed?)')
    if fg>=500 and fg/max(fr,1)>=8: s+=25; r.append(f'ratio {fg}/{fr}')
    elif fg>=1500 and fr<200: s+=20; r.append(f'mass-follow {fg}/{fr}')
    if tw<=15 and fg>=200: s+=20; r.append(f'{tw} posts')
    elif tw<=5: s+=10; r.append(f'{tw} posts')
    if age is not None: s+=20 if age<60 else 10 if age<180 else 0; age<180 and r.append(f'{age}d old')
    if DIGITS.search(h): s+=10; r.append('generated handle')
    if md<=2 and lk>=500 and tw<=20 and fg>=500: s+=10; r.append('likes only')
    if u.get('verified'): s=max(0,s-15)
    # report gate: only report impersonation when the name or bio uses a real identity
    report_ok=bool(cb or cn or claim)
    return {'report_ok':report_ok,'username':h,'name':n,'score':s,'type':t if s>=30 else 'low','reason':'; '.join(r),'followers':fr,'following':fg,'posts':tw,'age_days':age,'bio':b[:160]}
if __name__=='__main__':
    src=Path(sys.argv[1]); d=json.loads(src.read_text()); users=d if isinstance(d,list) else d.get('data',[])
    out=sorted((score(u) for u in users),key=lambda x:-x['score'])
    Path(sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv)>2 else 'scored.json').write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2))
    for x in out[:20]: print(x['score'],'@'+x['username'],x['type'],'REPORT-OK' if x['report_ok'] else '',x['reason'])
```
Usage: `python3 score_followers.py profiles.json scored.json`. Neighbor batches for the network score use the same scorer; `report_ok` marks impersonators worth an X report.

routines.name: Weekly X follower review
routines.description: Fires weekly to review the owner's newest X followers and deliver a shortlist of suspected bots, reply-spam bots, and impersonators for approval.
routines.content:
Run the X follower review skill for the account in /workspace/x-guard/config.json. Follow that skill and the config file; do not hard-code personal handles in this prompt.

Use /workspace/x-guard/ for snapshots, blocked.txt, scored outputs, and reports. Prefer code and public X lookups; use the signed-in browser only to scrape follower and (for network score) neighbor lists.

Include the reply-spam check: for the top suspects, pull ~10 recent posts with one from:HANDLE search and run /workspace/x-guard/reply_spam.py. Tag accounts that paste the same canned reply under many different people's posts as reply-spam; per config.report_policy, these get reported as Spam (as well as blocked) once approved. Tag impersonators the scorer marks report_ok as reportable; other impersonation suspects are block-only. Porn/adult bots are blocked only, never reported.

Nothing is blocked, muted, reported, or unfollowed during the run; wait for the owner's approval of specific handles.

Send the result to the owner in this chat. Also send the same handle list to the assistant named in config.cc_assistant, if set.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 17 9 * * 3`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
